items.failure: Official OpenAI docs MCP registration could not start.
items.cause: An unrelated user-global Codex config value has an invalid service_tier.
items.repair: The global file was not changed; official OpenAI developer pages were used.
items.revalidation: Responses API, gpt-5.6-terra, and Structured Outputs contracts were verified from official sources.

items.failure: Windows PowerShell did not support Get-Date -AsUTC.
Initial dynamic-route source inspection treated [id] as a wildcard.
Initial hybrid typecheck reported duplicate metadata and narrow unions/mocks.
items.cause: New provider boundaries were more strictly typed than the first implementation.
items.repair: Removed the duplicate field and narrowed providers and mock response types.

items.failure: The first OpenAI validator used top-level await under a CommonJS tsx path.
items.repair: Wrapped validators in async main functions.
items.revalidation: Absent-key validation exits with the documented code 78.

items.failure: The first report-generator typecheck received unparsed string environment values.
items.cause: The internal router requires the typed runtime contract.
items.repair: Passed the values through the production Zod parser.

items.failure: One new release test expected the shortened phrase 'When GPT is used'.
items.cause: Test copy did not match the required UI title 'When GPT-5.6 is used'.
items.repair: Corrected the assertion without changing the product.

items.failure: The first browser filter scope assumed a named complementary region.
items.cause: The region had a visible heading but no accessible name.
items.repair: Used the unique labeled Work mode combobox from a fresh snapshot.
items.revalidation: REMOTE filtering reduced the catalog to three roles and excluded the onsite role.

items.failure: The first tracker navigation locator matched both header and contextual links.
items.cause: Two links shared the same href.
items.repair: Used the unique visible 'View Tracker' accessible name after a fresh snapshot.
items.revalidation: Save, tracker persistence, and restore pass.

items.failure: The first media-render script did not parse in Windows PowerShell 5.
items.cause: An en dash in a source message was decoded with the legacy shell code page.
items.repair: Kept the output UTF-8 but changed the script diagnostic to ASCII.

items.failure: The first MP4 passed codec and duration checks but visual spot checks found stitched full-page screenshot artifacts.
items.cause: The in-app browser's very tall full-page captures repeated sticky layout tiles.
items.repair: Replaced the affected segments with original on-brand release slides and one clean certified product crop, then rerendered.
items.revalidation: Frames at 5, 50, 100, 145, and 165 seconds pass visual inspection; H.264 video, AAC narration, embedded English captions, and 170-second duration pass.

items.failure: The final secret scanner initially matched the literal <server-secret> documentation placeholder.
items.cause: The placeholder used assignment syntax intentionally caught by the strict environment-secret pattern.
items.repair: Changed the exact clearance example to equivalent PowerShell Set-Item syntax without weakening the scanner.
items.revalidation: The complete public-safe mirror scan reports zero findings.
